description:
Team Description – VARSHA AI

We are a passionate and enthusiastic team of students participating in the NASA Hackathon with a mission to use technology and Earth observation data to address real-world agricultural challenges.

Our project, VARSHA AI, aims to support farmers affected by irregular and insufficient rainfall through accessible weather information, rainfall insights, drought monitoring, satellite-based observations, and crop advisory.
summary:
> JalVayu360 is a farmer-friendly web platform that converts complex NASA data into simple, actionable guidance for Indian farmers.
> 
> Farmers face uncertain rainfall, water stress, and technical information they cannot use. JalVayu360 solves this by using NASA POWER for weather and temperature, GPM-IMERG for rainfall, and SMAP for soil moisture. A farmer simply selects his village and gets current weather, rainfall risk, soil moisture, and simple guidance in easy language.
> 
> The platform also includes JalVayu AI, where farmers can ask questions like "Should I sow now?" and get a simple answer based on weather and soil data. Our goal is better planning, better water awareness, and a climate-aware farm. We did not just make a website, we made a tool that a real farmer can use
details: JalVayu360 is a smart agricultural platform that helps farmers make better daily decisions using NASA satellite data.What does it do? Farmer selects his village and gets temperature, rainfall, soil moisture, and crop risk in simple language. It shows a live map with colour cards - green for safe, yellow for caution, red for risk. Farmer can ask JalVayu AI chatbot questions like "Should I sow now?" and get a simple answer.How does it work? We use NASA POWER for weather, GPM-IMERG for rainfall, and SMAP for soil moisture. We clean the data, calculate risk, and show it on a simple mobile-friendly dashboard. No login needed.Tools used: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet for map, NASA POWER, GPM-IMERG, SMAP, and Gemini API for chatbot.Impact: Better planning, water awareness, and climate-aware farming. It helps small farmers save water, avoid crop loss, and decide the right time for sowing and irrigation.
